QUOTE: "Calls `client.createPost` again, sending a new post built from the local record." and "Retry is manual, one attempt per tap. Nothing re-sends in the background." and "On failure, sets `failed: true` again, unless it is one of the three removal errors above, in which case the post is deleted."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says `retryFailedPost` makes a single new `createPost` attempt per tap, marks the post failed again on error, and removes it for the same three errors. It also says the client send uses `retryLimit: 0`, so there is no loop or backoff.
